svg.title: Thinking Matter: From Vent Protocells to Planetary AI — All 68 Stops Across 4.1 Billion Years in 7 Acts
svg.desc: Clickable isometric switchback staircase across 7 Acts and all 68 stops of Earth’s history. Hover over any stop circle to read a brief description and click through to that stop.

g.text: From Vent Protocells to Planetary AI · 68 Stops in 7 Acts
Follow all 68 stops across Earth’s 4.1-billion-year census—from rock pores to 100,000-GPU clusters.
Hover over any stop circle for a brief description and link; each flight adds a new regime without erasing older ones.
HOVER ANY CIRCLE · CLICK TO OPEN ↗

a.aria-label: Act I: Ignition — jump to stop

a.data-hook: A mineral wall with a battery across it. Warm vent fluid meets acid ocean, and chemistry starts keeping score.
a.aria-label: Stop 1 of 68: Vent protocell, 4.1 Ga

a.data-hook: The ribosome arrives: a machine that reads a tape of codons and builds what it reads.
a.aria-label: Stop 2 of 68: LUCA, 3.8 Ga
Act II: Learning to swim in time — jump to stop

a.data-hook: A cell compares now with four seconds ago and swims toward food. Earth's first working memory.
a.aria-label: Stop 3 of 68: Swimming bacterium, 3.2 Ga

a.data-hook: A protein clock ticks once a day. The planning horizon jumps from seconds to 24 hours.
a.aria-label: Stop 4 of 68: Cyanobacterium, 2.9 Ga

a.data-hook: Oxygen poisons the old world and the planet freezes.
a.aria-label: Stop 5 of 68: The big freeze, 2.45 Ga, planetary crisis

a.data-hook: Breathing oxygen yields 15–18× more energy from each sugar.
a.aria-label: Stop 6 of 68: Oxygen-breathing bacterium, 2.1 Ga
Act III: The complex cell — jump to stop

a.data-hook: One cell swallows another and keeps it as a power plant.
a.aria-label: Stop 7 of 68: First complex cell, 1.8 Ga

a.data-hook: An eyespot wired to two flagella steers toward light in milliseconds.
a.aria-label: Stop 8 of 68: Green alga, 1.5 Ga

a.data-hook: Sex turns evolution into a parallel search.
a.aria-label: Stop 9 of 68: Red alga, 1.1 Ga

a.data-hook: Synapse proteins show up long before any synapse.
a.aria-label: Stop 10 of 68: Choanoflagellate colony, 900 Ma

a.data-hook: Ice from pole to equator for 55 million years. Living biomass falls 86%.
a.aria-label: Stop 11 of 68: Snowball Earth, 650 Ma, planetary crisis

a.data-hook: Melting ice washes ground-up rock into the sea. Sponges coordinate pumping across a whole body with chemical waves and no nerves.
a.aria-label: Stop 12 of 68: Demosponge, 635 Ma

a.data-hook: Bodies without nerves still coordinate, using peptides and voltage.
a.aria-label: Stop 13 of 68: Trichoplax & Charnia, 575 Ma

a.data-hook: Neurons are at work by now. Planet-wide synaptic activity goes from zero to 10²⁰ events per second.
a.aria-label: Stop 14 of 68: First worm, 555 Ma
Act IV (1/2): Eyes, brains, myelin, land — jump to stop

a.data-hook: Steering: approach the good, avoid the bad, in three dimensions.
a.aria-label: Stop 15 of 68: Burrowing worm, 541 Ma

a.data-hook: Eyes with 16,000 lenses start an arms race. Neural activity hits 800× its earlier level.
a.aria-label: Stop 16 of 68: Anomalocaris, 518 Ma

a.data-hook: Jet-propelled squid cousins hunt open water while coral clones wire vast reefs. Sea animal families triple and nerve activity jumps sixfold.
a.aria-label: Stop 17 of 68: Giant orthocone, 470 Ma

a.data-hook: Dopamine teaches by surprise. Brains learn from reward.
a.aria-label: Stop 18 of 68: Jawless fish, 455 Ma

a.data-hook: Ice returns. Most sea species die and neural activity falls 90%.
a.aria-label: Stop 19 of 68: First mass extinction, 445 Ma, planetary crisis

a.data-hook: Life refills the post-ice seas. Early fishes sense water ripples along their flanks and fire split-second escape flips.
a.aria-label: Stop 20 of 68: Sea scorpion, 440 Ma
Act IV (2/2): Eyes, brains, myelin, land — jump to stop

a.data-hook: Myelin insulates nerves: 50× faster signals for a hundredth of the energy.
a.aria-label: Stop 21 of 68: Jawed fish, 425 Ma

a.data-hook: Plants spread across the land and start piling up wood, a huge carbon store with almost no living cells.
a.aria-label: Stop 22 of 68: Early land plant, 400 Ma

a.data-hook: Runoff from the first forests starves the sea of oxygen. About 75% of marine species die, including giant armored fish, and nerve activity drops 70%.
a.aria-label: Stop 23 of 68: Armored fish collapse, 375 Ma, planetary crisis

a.data-hook: Eyes leave the water. Visible space grows a millionfold, and planning starts to pay.
a.aria-label: Stop 24 of 68: Walking fish, 365 Ma

a.data-hook: Oxygen near 30% powers giant insects over the coal forests.
a.aria-label: Stop 25 of 68: Giant dragonfly, 320 Ma

a.data-hook: A waterproof shelled egg frees vertebrates from water, and a three-layered forebrain maps dry inland Pangaea.
a.aria-label: Stop 26 of 68: First land reptile, 253 Ma
Act V (1/3): Extinctions and warm brains — jump to stop

a.data-hook: Super-volcanoes erupt. Biomass falls 76% and neural activity 94%.
a.aria-label: Stop 27 of 68: The Great Dying, 251.9 Ma, planetary crisis

a.data-hook: In thin 14%-oxygen air, mammal ancestors grow tactile whiskers and warm nose scrolls while dinosaur cousins evolve one-way lungs.
a.aria-label: Stop 28 of 68: Burrowing cynodont, 247 Ma

a.data-hook: A two-million-year rainy spell reshapes the land. Fast-running early dinosaurs balance on two legs, and global nerve signaling quadruples.
a.aria-label: Stop 29 of 68: Two-legged dinosaur, 230 Ma

a.data-hook: Warm blood and a layered cortex let small animals hunt at night and replay their routes.
a.aria-label: Stop 30 of 68: Night-shift mammal, 205 Ma

a.data-hook: Huge eruptions along the opening Atlantic fill the air with carbon dioxide. About 76% of species die, clearing the stage for giant dinosaurs.
a.aria-label: Stop 31 of 68: Rift volcanoes, 201 Ma, planetary crisis

a.data-hook: Old jaw bones begin to become a three-bone middle ear for high-pitched hearing.
a.aria-label: Stop 32 of 68: Paperclip-sized mammal, 185 Ma
Act V (2/3): Extinctions and warm brains — jump to stop

a.data-hook: Flight needs a fast 3D controller, so the brain's balance centers grow.
a.aria-label: Stop 33 of 68: Feathered flyer, 150 Ma

a.data-hook: Petals, scent and nectar turn flying insects into targeted pollen couriers, transforming land ecosystems.
a.aria-label: Stop 34 of 68: First flowers & pollinators, 125 Ma

a.data-hook: Ant and bee colonies act as superorganisms. Neural activity peaks at 2×10²⁶ events per second.
a.aria-label: Stop 35 of 68: T. rex and ant colonies, 66 Ma

a.data-hook: Impact winter. Neural activity falls 92.5% and the big dinosaurs are gone.
a.aria-label: Stop 36 of 68: Asteroid impact, 66 Ma, planetary crisis

a.data-hook: Small warm-blooded survivors inherit an emptied world.
a.aria-label: Stop 37 of 68: Early primate, 64.5 Ma
Act V (3/3): Extinctions and warm brains — jump to stop

a.data-hook: Forward-facing eyes spread through hothouse forests, some mammal brains begin to fold, and global nerve signaling more than doubles.
a.aria-label: Stop 38 of 68: Leaping primate, 50 Ma

a.data-hook: Whales see with sound; songbirds pack 240 million neurons into each gram of brain.
a.aria-label: Stop 39 of 68: Echolocating whale & songbird, 34 Ma

a.data-hook: Deep-diving sperm whales evolve Earth's largest brains and ocean-spanning click dialects while grasslands spread.
a.aria-label: Stop 40 of 68: Sperm-whale vocal clans, 20 Ma

a.data-hook: Reading minds: a prefrontal cortex that models what others know.
a.aria-label: Stop 41 of 68: Great ape, 10 Ma

a.data-hook: Drying African grasslands reward walking on two legs, freeing hands to carry while elephant and ape families coordinate across kilometers.
a.aria-label: Stop 42 of 68: Upright hominin, 7 Ma
Act VI (1/3): Memory leaves the body — jump to stop

a.data-hook: A struck stone keeps a plan for 10,000 years at zero watts. Memory leaves the body.
a.aria-label: Stop 43 of 68: Australopithecus, 3.3 Ma

a.data-hook: Sharp Oldowan stone flakes butcher meat and marrow, co-evolving with hand-eye brain circuits and multiplying memory outside bodies tenfold.
a.aria-label: Stop 44 of 68: Stone-flake maker, 2.5 Ma

a.data-hook: Possibly tending fire already: cooking digests food outside the body and frees energy for a bigger brain.
a.aria-label: Stop 45 of 68: Homo erectus, 1.5 Ma

a.data-hook: Modern-sized brains plan multi-step stone cores and balanced wooden spears, hunting big game in tight cooperative families.
a.aria-label: Stop 46 of 68: Spear-hunting band, 400 ka

a.data-hook: Early Homo sapiens across Africa combine modern-sized skulls, prepared-core stone blades and three-generation family care.
a.aria-label: Stop 47 of 68: First Homo sapiens, 315 ka

a.data-hook: Cross-hatched red ochre and pierced shell beads hold shared meaning outside the skull, multiplying external memory tenfold.
a.aria-label: Stop 48 of 68: Ochre engraver, 75 ka

a.data-hook: Language at ~39 bits per second, cave art and tally bones.
a.aria-label: Stop 49 of 68: Ice-age speakers & artists, 45 ka
Act VI (2/3): Memory leaves the body — jump to stop

a.data-hook: Domesticated grain and herds turn sunlight into stored surplus, anchoring permanent villages of thousands of people.
a.aria-label: Stop 50 of 68: First villagers, 10 ka

a.data-hook: Traders seal counting tokens inside hollow clay balls and press their shapes outside: three-dimensional objects become flat signs.
a.aria-label: Stop 51 of 68: Clay token envelope, ~4000 BCE

a.data-hook: Baked clay keeps records for thousands of years without power.
a.aria-label: Stop 52 of 68: Sumerian scribe, ~3000 BCE

a.data-hook: Shrinking ~800 word-signs down to 22 sound-letters makes reading far easier to learn and spreads literacy along Bronze Age trade routes.
a.aria-label: Stop 53 of 68: Alphabet & oracle bone, ~1300 BCE

a.data-hook: Panini writes ~4,000 exact rules for Sanskrit, Greeks prove geometry step by step, and stamped coins coordinate markets through prices.
a.aria-label: Stop 54 of 68: Grammar & proof, ~475 BCE

a.data-hook: Cataloged libraries hold tens of thousands of scrolls or more, bronze gears predict eclipses, and road-linked empires grow toward ~60 million people each.
a.aria-label: Stop 55 of 68: Antikythera & Alexandria, ~275 BCE
Act VI (3/3): Memory leaves the body — jump to stop

a.data-hook: Bound pages with numbers and tables of contents replace scrolls, letting readers jump straight to any passage instead of unrolling.
a.aria-label: Stop 56 of 68: The bound book, 426 CE

a.data-hook: Rag-paper mills spread across Eurasia while numbers with a zero turn hard arithmetic into quick, repeatable written algorithms.
a.aria-label: Stop 57 of 68: Paper mills & zero, 1026 CE

a.data-hook: Copying cost falls 300× and science becomes shared memory.
a.aria-label: Stop 58 of 68: Printing press, 1450 CE

a.data-hook: Geared calculators add and multiply by turning drums, while the first science journals make discoveries public and checkable.
a.aria-label: Stop 59 of 68: Stepped Reckoner & journal, 1665 CE

a.data-hook: Signals cross continents two million times faster than a nerve.
a.aria-label: Stop 60 of 68: Telegraph, 1844 CE

a.data-hook: Electric pins read holes in paper cards to count 63 million people in the 1890 US census, while radio sends signals without wires.
a.aria-label: Stop 61 of 68: Punch-card tabulator, 1890 CE
Act VII: Silicon — jump to stop

a.data-hook: Computing goes electronic and software becomes data.
a.aria-label: Stop 62 of 68: ENIAC, 1945 CE

a.data-hook: Whole circuits etched onto single silicon chips launch Moore's law, paired with electronic DRAM memory and packet-switched ARPANET.
a.aria-label: Stop 63 of 68: Microchips & ARPANET, 1966 CE

a.data-hook: Digital storage nears every paper, film and vinyl archive ever made, and passes it two years later.
a.aria-label: Stop 64 of 68: The Web, 2000 CE

a.data-hook: Smartphones put networked cameras and maps in a billion pockets while chemists boot the first synthetic bacterial genome.
a.aria-label: Stop 65 of 68: Smartphones & synthetic cell, 2010 CE

a.data-hook: Graphics chips get repurposed to learn.
a.aria-label: Stop 66 of 68: Deep learning, 2012 CE

a.data-hook: One self-attention neural architecture learns to write text and code and predicts the 3D shapes of 200 million biological proteins.
a.aria-label: Stop 67 of 68: Transformer & AlphaFold, 2020 CE

a.data-hook: One machine runs 3×10²⁰ operations per second. All silicon together is still 0.006% of animal brain activity, and the typical cell is still a bacterium.
a.aria-label: Stop 68 of 68: AI supercomputer, 2026 CE

g.text: Systema Intelligentiae · Quantitative 68-stop planetary census across 10 functional parts (4.1 Ga – 2026 CE).
Equal-sized steps show order of arrival, not equal time spans or species rank. Specimen plates openly licensed (CC0 / Public Domain / CC BY / CC BY-SA; full credits in credits.html).
